scope: Cell-level review of §12.3.2.2 destination arrays and Table 149, including null/zero operands, page target forms, model parsing, and observable geometry routes. Prior name-tree precedence, transformed rotation/crop coordinates, FitR/FitB centering, and cross-document action-view failures are reconciled as existing findings rather than reopened.

source.locator: ISO 32000-2:2020 §12.3.2.1–.2 and Table 149, printed pp.441–443 / primary PDF physical pp.456–458. The correct table number is 149 (Table 151 is unrelated).
effective_rules: A destination specifies the page, the window location on that page, and magnification. Following a destination presents the view it specifies.

Ordinary destination arrays name a page by indirect page reference. For GoToR and GoToE arrays the first element is instead an integer page number in the target document, zero-based; the 2020 correction note in §12.3.2.2 explicitly includes embedded Go-To as well as remote Go-To.
All Table 149 coordinates are in default user space. For FitB, FitBH, and FitBV, the smallest rectangle enclosing page content is bounded by the CropBox as specified in §12.3.2.2.

/XYZ has left, top, and zoom; null retains each current component independently, and zoom zero has null semantics. /Fit takes no operands. /FitH takes top; /FitV takes left; /FitR takes left, bottom, right, top; /FitB takes no operands; /FitBH takes top; /FitBV takes left.

/FitH and /FitBH fit width; /FitV and /FitBV fit height. The /FitB family uses the content bounding box. /Fit and /FitR fit both dimensions. The separate existing B24 review covers centering in unused dimensions. EC3 Issue #536 inserts “interactive processors should” before “use the smaller ... , centring the rectangle ...” in the same FitR sentence. Grammatically this makes both smaller-factor choice and centering a SHOULD-level recommendation for interactive processors. It does not change the separate unamended FitB imperative.
source.errata: Primary annotation checked at physical p.457 / printed p.442: Issue #536 Caret inserts 'interactive processors should' in the Table 149 FitR smaller-factor instruction. It is a recommendation, not a SHALL. No Table 149 erratum changing the eight form names or the XYZ null/zero semantics was found in physical pp.456–458. The embedded GoTo integer exception is recorded by the corrected §12.3.2.2 note.

cells.source_rule: Indirect page reference for ordinary destinations; integer index in the target for GoToR/GoToE, starting at zero.
cells.implementation: pdf-model::Destination retains PageTarget and resolves ordinary references in the current document; RemoteGoTo/GoToE resolve integer page indexes against the target page list.
cells.assertions: pdf-model destination tests distinguish local page references from remote integer targets. cross_document_destination_view_spec_audit has exact-xref local, remote, and embedded fixtures selecting page index 2, plus direct-target and local controls.
cells.status: Page selection is independently asserted. The separate B23 finding is that GoToR/GoToE drop the destination View while replacing the document; this review does not duplicate that finding.

cells.source_rule: Each null left/top/zoom retains the current component; zoom 0 is equivalent to null.
cells.implementation: pdf-model::destination::View::read maps null and zoom 0 to None; viewer-core::Open::apply_view retains the unstated corner/zoom.
cells.assertions: destination.rs::a_null_parameter_is_not_a_zero separates null and zero coordinates from stated numeric zeros. viewer-core/tests/destinations_residual_audit.rs checks retained state after navigation and an explicit-view control; headless.rs checks stated XYZ scale and origin.
cells.status: Parser and public local-navigation assertions use literal values and controls; no new gap established.

cells.source_rule: Fit the whole page in both dimensions and center unused space.
cells.implementation: Open::apply_view computes the min width/height fit and places the whole page.
cells.assertions: headless.rs::an_open_action_states_where_to_look_at_the_page_and_how_large checks a 600×800 page in a 300×400 window at scale 0.5; an independent whole-page spare-height control is recorded in destinations_current_followup/parent-review.json.
cells.status: Covered for the source-derived whole-page fit case.

cells.source_rule: Fit the page width or height, respectively; place the coordinate at the corresponding window edge, retaining it if null.
cells.implementation: Open::apply_view fits the selected page dimension and transforms stated user-space coordinates.
cells.assertions: headless.rs has independent FitH scale and top-coordinate values. destinations_residual_audit.rs compares FitV against its fitted crop height and computes the non-origin CropBox transform independently; null retention controls are in the same public integration family.
cells.status: Covered by literal public geometry and contrasting page-versus-content controls.

cells.source_rule: Fit the specified rectangle; the same Table 149 sentence says to use the smaller factor and center in unused space. EC3 #536 inserts SHOULD before that sentence, so this is recommended for interactive processors rather than an unqualified SHALL.
cells.implementation: View parser preserves four coordinates; Open::apply_view fits both dimensions and currently places a rectangle corner at the viewport corner.
cells.assertions: headless.rs has matched-aspect and literal centered-geometry assertions. Parent review of destinations_current_followup records the unused-dimension case failing against the recommended centering behavior and the matched-aspect control passing.
cells.status: Existing B24 records an implementation mismatch with the recommended FitR behavior, not a mandatory ISO “shall” violation. No new array-cell finding.

cells.source_rule: Fit the page-content bounding box, clipped to CropBox; center placement is covered by B24.
cells.implementation: Open::apply_view derives a content box and currently places its upper-left corner at the viewport corner.
cells.assertions: headless.rs uses a one-rectangle content fixture. Parent's B24 review adds vertical/horizontal unused-dimension assertions and matched-aspect controls; the center case fails.
cells.status: Existing B24 finding; bounded to centering in unused dimension.

cells.source_rule: Fit content bounding-box width or height; stated top/left coordinates remain default-user-space placement operands.
cells.implementation: View::FitBH/FitBV retain the coordinate; apply_view maps it through the page transform and fits the selected content dimension.
cells.assertions: destinations_residual_audit.rs::fitbh_fits_the_content_width_and_places_top_in_default_user_space and ::fitbv_fits_the_content_height_and_transforms_left_from_user_space assert independent coordinate arithmetic and contrast each with FitH/FitV page-box controls.
cells.status: Public geometry assertions independently discriminate content bounds from page bounds; no new gap found.

selected_adrs: ADR 0162: local destination view representation and geometry; retain supported page/zoom claims but do not repeat the previously reviewed FitR/FitB centering rationale.

ADR 2814: default-space coordinates and null retention; current local geometry tests support these narrow claims. Rotation/crop composition is already reviewed in navigation_geometry_residual_current.
ADR 1227 and ADR 0094: remote request boundary and embedded traversal are not reevaluated here; B23 already isolates view loss from page selection/traversal.

limits: B24 must be described as a FitR SHOULD-level discrepancy for interactive processors under the grammatical scope of #536; its FitB cases remain governed by the unamended Table 149 imperative.

No new tests are proposed: all eight forms have model parsing coverage, all meaningful local geometry variants are exercised through public consumers, and prior shards already contain controls for CropBox coordinates and cross-document page selection.
The model test's all-eight assertion proves parsing only; geometry confidence comes from the separate public assertions listed above.
This review does not certify malformed operand recovery, every fit form under every page transform, external-target UI handoff, or visual/native host behavior.
B23 and B24 remain separately recorded issues; this feature-cell inventory neither fixes nor restates their full arguments.
